rationale: This sample is a tiny Shootout benchmark (4 functions, 292 text bytes) whose only interesting target is the hot recursive fib routine, so the table favors cheap, low-risk transformations that still degrade static analysis: SUB (instruction substitution) and ICALL (indirect calls) get the highest security/diversity weights because they obscure arithmetic and call structure at negligible cost; IGV keeps constant/global visibility low with essentially no runtime penalty, which suits a size- and speed-constrained binary; SPLIT and IBR are kept at moderate weights to add basic-block and branch diversity without inflating the 292-byte text section. BCF and FLA are deliberately damped: bogus control flow roughly multiplies body size and flattening imposes dispatch overhead on every loop iteration, which is exactly the wrong trade for a hot recursive kernel where runtime overhead must stay acceptable, so their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are kept low so cost-sensitive features do not drive their application, while a slightly elevated CorrectnessRisk on BCF further biases the selector away from it on this minimal, correctness-critical sample.
